title: Repertoire of the Thibodaux dance bands
summary: They played waltzes, quadrilles, blues and stock arrangements, including 'Ho Alley Ho' and High Society, and many numbers by ear.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Did they ever play any of the old blues up there? Or was it mostly written music? How did you remember? Well, uh, they... For any of the dances, not just the Gabriel Benth, or any other dances around? Any type, what type of music, the pieces that they played? Did they play like waltzes or marches or foxtrotts or quadrilles? Or what kind of music was it like?
They played waltzes, quadrilles, and they played blues, and they played stock music. At that time.
Most of the music they used was written, I mean arranged the stock arrangements that they...

Yeah, they would always arrange it. Today ideas were not as great as the, you would say, the modern arrangement, that they would arrange it, that they could play it and they would always play it. That way they had the feelings of playing their music. Yeah.
They played the St. Louis Blues.
And I recall that they played a blues they called Ho, Alley Ho. I don't know if you ever heard of that.
Yeah, well, that's what they called it at that time. If your house catch a fire, throw your trunk out the window.
Well, they played blues at that time, like that. They played high society, numbers, like that. It was practically on the same order, like, fear on that.
Yeah. Did they ever play any routine or stuff just by the ear?
Oh yeah, yeah. The arrangement, this was occasionally at that time, or something that they wasn't so familiar with and when they learned it, but they played a lot of numbers without music.
Yeah, that's why I wondered how that...
